summary: SCIM provisioning fails after device client-cert rotation: percent-encoded CN rejected by identity-proxy
description:
Issue summary: After a scheduled device client-certificate rotation in Nimbus Analytics' private deployment, SCIM provisioning requests started failing with 401/403 between the customer's provisioning service and Redwood's identity-proxy. Impact: New user and group provisioning is blocked; onboarding flows that rely on SCIM are failing for ~12% of new users, customer-facing admin console shows missing role bindings for recent accounts. Environment: Private deployment (VPC) in us-west-2, Redwood control plane (private), customer-managed device client certs used for SCIM client authentication via mTLS to identity-proxy.

Observed behavior: SCIM POST/PATCH requests are rejected by identity-proxy with TLS-level client authentication success but identity-proxy returns 403 due to inability to map certificate subject to service account. Logs show the parsed certificate CN contains percent-encoded characters ("CN=John%2EDoe@nimbus.example.com") after the rotation; internal name-normalization routine rejects non-alphanumeric characters and falls into the "unmapped" path.

Expected behavior: Certificate CN should be accepted if it matches the documented service account projection format; percent-encoded values should either be decoded or normalized by identity-proxy to map to the correct service account.

Impact severity: High — provisioning outages for new accounts and missed role assignments; customer has paused onboarding and requesting urgent remediation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In a private deployment, rotate device client certs for a SCIM client where the issuing tooling URL-encodes special characters into certificate CN.
2) Trigger SCIM provisioning event from customer provisioning service (POST /scim/v2/Users or PATCH groups) authenticated via mTLS.
3) Observe identity-proxy logs and SCIM response codes returned to the provisioning client.
4) Check resulting user existence and role bindings in the Redwood admin console and SCIM audit logs.
logs: 2026-03-12T09:21:43Z identity-proxy INFO: TLS client auth succeeded: subject=CN=John%2EDoe@nimbus.example.com,O=Nimbus,C=US
2026-03-12T09:21:43Z identity-proxy WARN: Subject normalization failed: invalid characters in CN 'John%2EDoe@nimbus.example.com'
2026-03-12T09:21:43Z scim-handler ERROR: Service account lookup returned EMPTY -> returning 403 for request id=aa12b3
comments: 2026-03-12 10:05 - Support (Asha Patel): Logged after initial customer report; requesting provisioning client cert subject example and rotation time.
2026-03-12 11:12 - Customer (Nimbus): Provided cert PEM and rotation logs; their cert issuance pipeline URL-encodes '.' to '%2E' for legacy reasons.
2026-03-12 13:40 - SRE (Mateo Rivera): Verified identity-proxy received client cert and that subject CN contains percent-encoding; attempting repro in staging with a cert containing '%2E' in CN.

2026-03-13 09:22 - Engineer (Leila Chen): Confirmed normalization function rejects characters outside [A-Za-z0-9@._-]; creating PR to decode percent-encoded sequences before validation. See PR linked.

2026-03-14 08:30 - Support (Asha Patel): Customer applied temporary workaround (re-issued certs with decoded CN) and provisioning resumed; customer requests a durable fix and a mitigation for future rotations.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Certificate issuance pipeline started URL-encoding certain characters ('.' -> '%2E') causing identity-proxy subject parser to treat CN as invalid and not map to service account projection.

Hypothesis 2: A recent hardening change to identity-proxy introduced stricter validation that no longer tolerates percent-encoded sequences; previous behavior silently decoded or accepted these values.
Evidence: Reproduced locally by generating cert with CN containing '%2E' -> identity-proxy normalization fails; reverting to decoded CN restores mapping.
Relevant code: identity-proxy/pkg/auth/subject_normalizer.go -> validateAndNormalizeSubject(); seen reject branch for '%' characters.
resolution: Workaround applied: Customer re-issued device client certificates with decoded CNs (replaced '%2E' with '.') and restarted their provisioning client; SCIM provisioning resumed and missing role bindings are being reconciled. Permanent fix: Engineering implemented PR to perform URL-decoding of percent-encoded sequences in certificate subject normalization and added unit tests for common encodings. Deployed identity-proxy patch to staging (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/789) and scheduled rollout to private control planes. Follow-ups: 1) We will publish a KB documenting certificate CN formatting recommendations for private deployments and update the rotation runbook. 2) Add a monitoring alert to detect spikes in 'subject_normalization_failed' log metric and auto-notify support.
follow_up_actions: Deploy identity-proxy fix to private control planes during next maintenance window (owner: Mateo Rivera).
Create KB article advising customers to avoid percent-encoding in cert CNs and provide cert generation examples (owner: Developer Experience).
Add unit/integration tests to provisioning CI to catch percent-encoded CNs (owner: Engineering).
Open automation ticket to run a scan for customer-managed certs with '%' in CN and notify impacted customers (owner: Support Ops).
